Ever wondered what goes into running a farm and sheep dairy? Join us for one of our fun and educational farm tours of Green Dirt Farm!

Get a guided look at our farm, a glimpse inside our milking parlor, and a view into our cheese kitchen. Then you’ll return to our shop for a guided tasting of our cheeses! We invite you to enjoy lunch or a snack from our Café after your tour!

SHIPPING POLICY

Perishables are expensive to ship.

We’re sorry, and we wish it wasn’t so, but there it is. Please be aware that we must ship 2nd Day (or overnight in hot weather) to areas that are more than 800 miles away from us, to make sure your cheese gets to you safe and sound. But…that doesn’t mean your cheese will arrive 2 days after you ordered it…that’s because we only ship on Mondays, Tuesdays and sometimes, (if we’re not too busy making cheese) Wednesdays. This ensures that your cheese won’t sit in a warehouse over the weekend. Orders placed after noon on Tuesday will ship the following week, unless you choose overnight shipping and let us know in your order notes that you need to receive the cheese asap.

If you’d like us to ship your items a different week just put the date or week you’d like your items to ship in your order notes. Thank you!!

A note about delayed shipments and other shipping mishaps: If your shipment arrives warm or damaged we will replace it free of charge. Please note that we do not issue refunds for shipping mishaps or delays.

We cannot deliver to a PO box.

You can minimize your shipping costs and still support us by buying our non-perishable items. Or you can maximize your cheese to shipping cost by buying more cheese (we like that option!). In fact, if you spend just $175 we will ship your package free of shipping charge!* Finally, here’s a hot tip to help with the high costs- every once in a while we send a coupon to folks who have signed up for our newsletter. So, quick- sign up!

*Free shipping not applicable to shipping destinations in Alaska or Hawaii.

HOW WE STARTED

Sarah Hoffmann was working as a doctor at the University of Washington when she started dreaming about running her own farm. She’d grown up on a farm and loved it, and her Aunt Jean—who ran a gourmet cheese shop back when women business owners were few and far between—inspired her to pursue both fine cheesemaking and entrepreneurship. In 2002, Sarah took the leap and started her dairy, beginning her journey of crafting sheep’s milk cheeses at Green Dirt Farm in Northwest Missouri.

Today, more than twenty-two years later, Sarah runs the farm alongside her daughter, Eliza, and a dedicated team. What started as a dairy has grown into a retail store and café, a restaurant, and agritourism experiences—all showcasing the cheeses we make right here in our cheese kitchen on our Animal Welfare Approved® farm. We’re living our dreams and doing the groundwork (literally!) to craft amazing cheese in a way that’s both humane and sustainable. We’re doing the groundwork (literally!) to craft fantastic cheese in a humane, sustainable way.

But don’t just take our word for it. Since we started making cheese commercially in 2008, we’ve earned over 90 awards from the artisan cheese community—including four at the 2025 American Cheese Society competition. In 2023, our Prairie Tomme (a hard sheep’s milk cheese) took 3rd place in Best in Show at the ACS competition, beating out over 1,400 American artisanal cheeses! Read more on our blog about our awards. We’ve also been honored to receive Good Food Awards in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2024, and 2025. And in 2021, Food & Wine named us among the 50 best cheesemakers in the US: https://www.foodandwine.com/lifestyle/best-cheese-america

THE BENEFITS OF SHEEP MILK
WHY SHEEP MILK?

Sheep milk is naturally rich, creamy and nutrient-dense, with A2 milk protein, beneficial fats, and more protein and calcium than cow milk. For many people, it may also offer an easier-to-digest alternative to conventional dairy.

Explore the Benefits

EASIER TO DIGEST

for many people

Love dairy, but find that cow’s milk doesn’t always love you back? Sheep milk offers a delicious alternative for people exploring dairy options that may be easier to digest.

Sheep milk differs naturally from cow’s milk in both its proteins and fats. Its proteins have different structures and digestive behavior, and sheep milk naturally contains only A2 beta-casein rather than the combination of A1 and A2 beta-casein commonly found in cow’s milk. Sheep milk is also naturally rich in short- and medium-chain fatty acids, which are broken down differently during digestion. Together, these differences may help explain why some people find sheep milk easier to tolerate than conventional cow’s milk.

Everyone’s digestion is different. 
Sheep milk still contains lactose and milk proteins, so it isn’t lactose-free and may not be suitable for people with a cow’s milk allergy.

NATURALLY A2 MILK PROTEIN
Conventional Cow Milk

A1 + A2

Sheep Milk

A2

Not all milk proteins are the same.

Beta-casein, one of the primary proteins in milk, occurs in several forms, including A1 and A2 milk. Most conventional cow’s milk contains a combination of A1 and A2 beta-casein, while sheep milk naturally contains only the A2 form.

Why does that matter? A2 dairy has gained attention because research suggests some people may experience less digestive discomfort with A2-only milk compared with conventional milk containing A1 protein. It’s one of the reasons people who have trouble with cow’s milk may be interested in exploring sheep dairy.

For Green Dirt Farm, A2 isn’t something we add or engineer. It’s simply a natural characteristic of sheep milk.

BENEFICIAL FATS

CLA • Omega-3 • Butyric Acid • MCTs

Sheep milk doesn’t just contain more milk solids than cow’s milk. It also has a distinctive mix of naturally occurring fats. Sheep milk is rich in short- and medium-chain fatty acids, which the body processes differently than longer-chain fats.

It also naturally contains beneficial fatty acids including conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), omega-3 fatty acids and butyric acid. Together, these contribute to sheep milk’s unique nutritional profile while also helping create the rich, creamy texture that makes sheep milk so delicious.

It’s another way sheep milk packs a lot of goodness into every serving.

PROTEIN + CALCIUM
50% More Protein
2x the Calcium

Sheep milk is naturally nutrient-dense, packing more protein, calcium and milk solids into every serving than cow’s milk. In fact, sheep milk typically provides substantially more protein and nearly twice the calcium of whole cow’s milk.

Protein helps build and maintain muscle, while calcium is essential for strong bones and teeth. That makes sheep milk a naturally nourishing choice whether you’re enjoying it as milk, creamy yogurt or fresh cheese.

More protein. More calcium. Naturally sheep milk.
